I am 60 this year, and I have farmed this land most of my life. I did not study much, so I do not sit and calculate like the technicians do. I look at what happened before, what the neighbors are doing, and what money I can safely spend. On my 9 mu, I cannot take big risks. Wheat and maize are the backbone because they feed the family and bring steady grain income. Cotton I keep on some land because I know how to manage it and if the price is decent it helps with cash. Watermelon I only keep on a small piece, because it can make money but it needs more care and if the weather turns bad or disease comes, losses come fast. Since I have a well, I am not as afraid of dry spells, but pumping costs money, so I do not irrigate unless the crop really needs it.

For wheat, I will follow the usual local timing and not change much. Last year when wheat had enough base fertilizer and one topdressing, yield was steadier, so I will do that again. After wheat harvest, maize must go in quickly, no delay, because in our place the turnaround is tight. I will not do heavy tillage there, just quick residue handling and sowing. Cotton I will keep simple, with moderate fertilizer and a few irrigations if dry. Watermelon gets the most attention per mu, but only on a small area so I can manage it with family labor. I will spend carefully: enough fertilizer so crops do not go hungry, but not too much because every extra bag is cash out of pocket.
